membership.name: Boston Health Care for the Homeless Program
membership.primaryEvidence: Boston clinic at 780 Albany Street and Greater Boston homeless-care sites; primary medical, respite, HIV/HCV and addiction services. Giving page names BHCHP Inc. and its EIN. Service partners are not extra recipients.

membership.name: Fenway Health
membership.primaryEvidence: Fenway provides medical, behavioral, HIV/STI and medication-assisted care at Boylston Street in Boston. Giving page identifies Fenway Health and EIN. Patients also travel from outside MA; whole-gift local fraction is not 100%. Homepage includes unrelated spam-like text, excluded from evidence.

membership.name: BAGLY
membership.primaryEvidence: BAGLY identifies itself as a 501(c)(3), with Boston youth community center at 28 Court Square, health/wellness and stabilization programs, and a current named donation page. Statewide AGLY network is not an additional recipient or all Boston benefit.

membership.name: Victory Programs
membership.primaryEvidence: Victory operates housing, recovery and prevention programs throughout Boston; Boston Living Center, HIV/HCV testing and overdose-prevention resources are within the same recipient. Official ways-to-give page specifies checks to Victory Programs and EIN.

membership.name: RIZE Massachusetts
membership.primaryEvidence: RIZE is a Massachusetts overdose-focused funder and convenor with current grants for harm reduction, care access and recovery; its named donation page supports the fund. Statewide policy/grant eligibility intersects all five MA MSA counties; grant dollars and recipient delivery must not be counted twice.

membership.name: Boston Medical Center
membership.primaryEvidence: BMC provides Boston safety-net clinical and addiction care; its development site names Boston Medical Center and EIN 04-3314093. Hospital and system expansion are not grounds to treat an ordinary gift as a restricted addiction grant or to omit full recipient expenses.

membership.name: Samaritans Inc.
membership.primaryEvidence: Samaritans Inc. is an independently operated Massachusetts nonprofit providing 988 calls/texts, Hey Sam youth text support, grief services and prevention education from Boston. Official giving page specifies EIN 04-2643466. Nationally accessible contacts are not all Boston-resident benefits.

membership.name: Bay State Community Services (including MOAR)
membership.primaryEvidence: MOAR's own donation page explicitly says it is a program of Bay State Community Services and gifts are received by BSCS for MOAR. BSCS primary site confirms recovery, behavioral and family programs. Count BSCS once, not a free-standing MOAR charity; statewide recovery advocacy applies to MA MSA residents.

membership.name: Learn to Cope
membership.primaryEvidence: Learn to Cope's current meeting list identifies Weymouth, Gloucester, Ipswich and Tewksbury groups. Free family support, overdose-response education and naloxone resources have an official giving path. Taunton HQ, western MA and Florida activities are outside this MSA.

membership.name: Gavin Foundation
membership.primaryEvidence: Gavin lists South Boston and Charlestown recovery houses, community recovery services, recovery coaches and substance-use treatment; donation page names Gavin Foundation and EIN. Count treatment and housing programs together; reported participants are not prevented deaths.

membership.name: Bay Cove Human Services
membership.primaryEvidence: Bay Cove lists addiction, mental-health, housing and disability services and explicitly includes CASPAR; official donations are to Bay Cove Human Services Inc. with EIN. Boston service network is in scope; CASPAR is not an independent extra recipient.

membership.name: Casa Esperanza
membership.primaryEvidence: Casa Esperanza provides culturally/linguistically adapted outpatient and inpatient substance-use/mental-health treatment, with Roxbury and Tewksbury service locations. Current giving page supports Casa. Keep residential, clinical and recovery supports inside the whole-recipient cost boundary.

membership.name: North Suffolk Community Services
membership.primaryEvidence: North Suffolk lists behavioral crisis, outpatient psychiatry, addiction and early-childhood programs serving Chelsea, East Boston, Revere, Roxbury, Winthrop and Charlestown. Official Donate button links a hosted form; its script-only destination was not transaction-tested.

membership.name: Riverside Community Care
membership.primaryEvidence: Riverside's current CBHC page lists Norwood care and eligible Norfolk/Middlesex communities including Dedham, Needham and Newton; it offers crisis response, outpatient care and MAT. Milford/Worcester-region activity is not all in boundary. Official giving page names Riverside Community Care.

membership.name: Vinfen
membership.primaryEvidence: Vinfen's services include Greater Lowell restoration services, clinical/crisis access, supported living and disability services; Cambridge headquarters and Greater Lowell delivery establish a local intersection. Official giving page names Vinfen and EIN. Connecticut and other MA work are not all Boston benefit.

membership.name: Eliot Community Human Services
membership.primaryEvidence: Eliot's current CBHC page specifies Lynn and Danvers clinics, urgent mental-health/substance-use treatment and crisis services. Giving page identifies Eliot as a nonprofit. Lexington HQ alone is not used as clinical benefit evidence; other statewide services require a separate local share.

membership.name: The Brookline Center for Community Mental Health
membership.primaryEvidence: Brookline Center provides counseling, care integration, housing support and early-psychosis/CEDAR services from Brookline, with a stated free/reduced-fee care component. Giving page names legal recipient Brookline Community Mental Health Center Inc. and EIN.

membership.name: The Home for Little Wanderers
membership.primaryEvidence: The Home lists child behavioral/clinical care, foster/adoption, schools and residential services, including current Greater Boston children and a Boston service history. Official personal-giving route identifies the Home nonprofit. Its New York and other non-MSA programs remain outside local benefit.

membership.name: Walker Therapeutic and Educational Programs
membership.primaryEvidence: Walker lists Needham intensive/residential/outpatient care, Watertown therapeutic schooling/after-school services and Roxbury girls programming. Official ways-to-give page supports Walker. Statewide referrals mean facility location does not imply all beneficiaries reside within this MSA.

membership.name: Italian Home for Children
membership.primaryEvidence: Italian Home for Children lists residential, outpatient, home/community mental-health programs and its Jamaica Plain school; official giving instructions name Italian Home at 1125 Centre Street. Program names are not separate recipients.

membership.name: Wayside Youth and Family Support Network
membership.primaryEvidence: Wayside identifies Framingham, Watertown and supported-living programs in Arlington, Somerville and Waltham, plus youth mental-health and family care. Its official EIN and giving page are explicit. Broad statewide program totals cannot all be credited locally.

membership.name: Justice Resource Institute
membership.primaryEvidence: JRI's current primary site identifies Rediscovery House in Waltham and a broad trauma/behavioral/social-service portfolio; giving page names JRI and EIN with program designations including STRIVE Boston. All non-MSA programs and full recipient resource costs remain material.

membership.name: The Dimock Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Dimock lists integrated health, behavioral care and addiction treatment on its Roxbury campus. Official support page names The Dimock Center and federal ID 04-3487827. The medical-health-center and umbrella structure must be reconciled at alpha rather than using a convenient small program budget.

membership.name: Codman Square Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Codman provides Dorchester primary/dental/behavioral care, substance-use services, urgent care and mobile services. Official giving page distinguishes gifts from insurer/government reimbursement. BMC-managed pharmacy is not a new recipient or a reason to attribute all pharmacy outcomes to Codman gifts.

membership.name: Whittier Street Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Whittier lists primary, behavioral, dental, eye and mobile care in Roxbury, regardless of ability to pay; official donation page is live. Its service footprint, rather than broad aspirational health-equity claims, is the discovery evidence.

membership.name: Mattapan Community Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Mattapan CHC identifies comprehensive community health care and an explicit request for gifts to support care in Mattapan and surrounding communities. Retrieved Donate page is a thank-you template, not proof a new payment can complete; official support intent is verified but donor checkout needs alpha recheck.

membership.name: Boston Area Rape Crisis Center
membership.primaryEvidence: BARCC offers free confidential counseling, medical advocacy, legal support and crisis contact for sexual-violence survivors. Its own site lists Cambridge and Boston walk-in sites and its ways-to-give page names the nonprofit. Its office at Casa Myrna is co-location, not a merger or an additional recipient.

membership.name: Upham's Corner Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Upham's Corner provides North Dorchester medical, behavioral, older-adult/PACE and home-health services. Donation page explains support for patient/community needs. PACE and other programs remain one recipient; local clients served are not QALYs.

membership.name: South Boston Community Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: South Boston CHC provides primary/preventive, behavioral and substance-use care and Seaport urgent care. Giving page names EIN and notes needs not fully covered by insurance, including transport and food. A gift is still whole-recipient support unless a restriction is documented.

membership.name: NeighborHealth
membership.primaryEvidence: Former South End CHC redirects to NeighborHealth's active South End site, 1601 Washington Street. NeighborHealth donation/about pages describe East Boston, South End, Revere, Winthrop and Everett care. Count current NeighborHealth recipient once, not South End plus East Boston separately.

membership.name: North End Waterfront Health
membership.primaryEvidence: NEW Health's own about and giving pages describe North End/Charlestown clinical sites, name the gift payee NEW Health and EIN 23-7089746, and distinguish affiliations with MGH and BMC. This separately identified recipient is not merged with BMC solely because of affiliation.

membership.name: Charles River Community Health
membership.primaryEvidence: Charles River CHC official giving page, retrieved through web indexing after direct 403, identifies tax-deductible gifts and Brighton/Waltham clinical locations with medical, dental, eye and behavioral care. Exact EIN is unverified here; the named recipient and care sites are not conjectural.

membership.name: Brockton Neighborhood Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Brockton Neighborhood HC provides medical, dental and substance-use care in Brockton and accepts gifts for services. Its primary page discloses major public/nonfederal program resources; gift marginality cannot be assumed from total patient volume.

membership.name: BAMSI
membership.primaryEvidence: BAMSI identifies itself as a Brockton-founded nonprofit with behavioral, substance-use, HIV, disability and early-childhood services. Its recipient-linked giving form permits service designations. One broad organization; an attractive program cannot supply a narrow cost denominator for unrestricted gifts. Final locality check: primary additional-programs page explicitly describes Brockton After School Enrichment therapeutic services for children ages 6-12.

membership.name: Greater Lawrence Family Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Greater Lawrence FHC serves Merrimack Valley patients with comprehensive care, pharmacy, outreach and enrollment assistance, with a current Lawrence service presence. Official giving page says gifts support patient transport and programs. Do not conflate NH Merrimack Valley residents with the MA scope.

membership.name: Greater Lynn Senior Services
membership.primaryEvidence: Greater Lynn Senior Services explicitly serves Lynn, Lynnfield, Nahant, Saugus and Swampscott with home care, meals, counseling and disability supports. Giving page identifies GLSS and EIN and distinguishes unrestricted gifts from named designations.

membership.name: Lynn Community Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Lynn CHC provides integrated primary, behavioral, dental, school and outreach care in Lynn; official giving page identifies LCHC nonprofit and EIN. Current expansion is a capacity lead, not a verified marginal funding gap or cost-effectiveness result.

membership.name: North Shore Community Health
membership.primaryEvidence: North Shore CHC identifies Salem, Gloucester and Peabody care sites, integrated medical/behavioral/dental services and a donation form supporting its care. School clinics and constituent locations are one recipient, not separate charities.

membership.name: Lowell Community Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Lowell CHC provides clinical and community wellness services across Greater Lowell, including behavioral health, HIV and substance-use services. Its current giving campaign seeks clinical access and workforce investment. Claims of patient scale do not establish additional gift-funded care.

membership.name: MetroWest Free Medical Program
membership.primaryEvidence: MetroWest Free Medical Program is an identified 501(c)(3), EIN 04-3822273, with current general/women's clinics in Marlborough and vision care in Sudbury. Giving supports clinical coordinators/interpreters and volunteer care; FQHC referrals are part of its counterfactual, not excluded alternatives.

membership.name: Health Imperatives
membership.primaryEvidence: Health Imperatives explicitly has Greater Brockton and Plymouth/South Shore locations, reproductive care, abortion services, harm reduction, survivor care and young-parent supports. Giving page specifies Health Imperatives and EIN. Cape/Islands/New Bedford activity is not Boston-MSA benefit.

membership.name: Planned Parenthood League of Massachusetts
membership.primaryEvidence: PPLM's official indexed contact page lists Greater Boston and Marlborough health centers and a PPLM development contact. Direct fetch is blocked; primary indexed content was checked. Affiliate clinical recipient is distinct from PPFA and the Massachusetts advocacy fund; Springfield/Worcester services are outside this MSA.

membership.name: Eastern Massachusetts Abortion Fund
membership.primaryEvidence: EMA Fund's own intake page accepts residents of or abortions in eastern Massachusetts, with prospective grants and logistics; applications do not guarantee funding. Its giving page names Eastern Massachusetts Abortion Fund Inc. and EIN. Nonresident travelers treated locally are not automatically resident-local health gains.

membership.name: Jane Doe Inc
membership.primaryEvidence: Jane Doe Inc. identifies a statewide sexual/domestic-violence coalition, active policy work and charitable giving. Its own page distinguishes coalition advocacy from member delivery. MA-wide law/program applicability intersects the five MA MSA counties, but no measured local-benefit share is asserted.

membership.name: REACH Beyond Domestic Violence
membership.primaryEvidence: REACH serves 27 MetroWest/Greater Boston communities with shelter, community advocacy and prevention, and is based in Waltham. The official give page is current. Precise town-level patient shares are not claimed; compare narrower survivor agencies and overlapping shelter referrals. Final locality check: its primary service-area page explicitly lists Waltham, Arlington, Newton, Needham and other Middlesex/Norfolk communities.

membership.name: Casa Myrna
membership.primaryEvidence: Casa Myrna describes Boston domestic-violence shelter/support services and the statewide SafeLink hotline; its named current hosted donor campaign supports survivor safety. SafeLink and co-located BARCC are not additional Casa Myrna recipients or additive causal outcomes.

membership.name: RESPOND Inc
membership.primaryEvidence: RESPOND provides Eastern MA survivor housing, shelter and counseling with a Somerville-area community footprint. Official giving page identifies RESPOND Inc. and EIN 51-0163763. Housing assistance and counseling require separate measured outcomes before adding health effects.

membership.name: HarborCOV
membership.primaryEvidence: HarborCOV provides Chelsea-area survivor housing, legal help and multilingual 24/7 advocacy. Its own site links a PayPal giving route. Service and named recipient are verified; the redirected script-limited payment screen was not transaction-verified.

membership.name: The Network La Red
membership.primaryEvidence: The Network/La Red provides partner-abuse survivor support, housing pathways, hotline and groups for LGBTQ+, kink and polyamorous communities from Boston. Its official giving page supports those services. Nationally accessible hotline reach is not assumed to be local residency.

membership.name: Jeanne Geiger Crisis Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Jeanne Geiger Crisis Center lists survivor/children's services in Amesbury and Lawrence and an official donation page. It directs national homicide-prevention work to Geiger Institute; the institute is not counted separately and no attribution of all national outcomes to the local gift is made.

membership.name: Healing Abuse Working for Change
membership.primaryEvidence: HAWC describes free confidential survivor support in 23 North Shore towns, including advocacy, counseling, children's services and shelter, with Salem location and an active donation page. Only local service intersection is counted; no official fundraising unit is accepted as a QALY cost.

membership.name: New Hope Inc
membership.primaryEvidence: New Hope's current office/court listing explicitly covers Bellingham through Milford court advocacy. This Norfolk service qualifies despite all main offices being outside the MSA. Most 41-town activity is outside scope; use full New Hope costs and only eligible local benefits.

membership.name: DOVE Inc
membership.primaryEvidence: DOVE lists Quincy/Dedham court outreach, survivor counseling, legal advocacy, shelter and a current donation page naming EIN 04-2667808. Whole-recipient support includes prevention/outreach as well as direct crisis services.

membership.name: Family and Community Resources
membership.primaryEvidence: Family and Community Resources identifies Brockton service offices, trauma/violence programs and current counseling/support activity. Its donation page specifies FCR Inc., EIN 04-2616114. A second EIN appearing for a third-party giving option is not used as FCR's identity.

membership.name: Greater Boston Legal Services
membership.primaryEvidence: GBLS explicitly provides free civil legal services for Greater Boston and operates Boston/Cambridge offices; housing, benefits, family safety and care-related rights are current mechanisms. Named giving page supports direct cases and systemic work; legal wins are not themselves clinical outcomes.

membership.name: De Novo Center for Justice and Healing
membership.primaryEvidence: De Novo is the former CLSACC, not a separate charity; official site/giving page identify EIN 04-2470335. Cambridge legal aid, disability/benefits access and counseling for trauma survivors offer a direct legal-plus-mental-health pathway without assuming every case produces health gains.

membership.name: MetroWest Legal Services
membership.primaryEvidence: MetroWest Legal's current eligibility page explicitly includes Framingham, Marlborough and Norfolk towns, with housing, benefits and medical-legal work. Insufficient staff can limit services to advice. Out-of-MSA senior services are excluded from local benefit; named giving route is verified.

membership.name: Northeast Legal Aid
membership.primaryEvidence: Northeast Legal Aid lists Lawrence, Lynn, Lowell and Haverhill offices and legal housing, benefits and medical-legal services. Its own site identifies subsidiary Northeast Justice Center; only NLA is counted and subsidiary/gift accounting must be reconciled before alpha.

membership.name: Disability Law Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Disability Law Center is Massachusetts' independent nonprofit protection-and-advocacy agency, with statewide legal access and current Bridgewater institutional-care advocacy. Official giving page identifies EIN. Count statewide policy applicability, not all MA program results as Boston health benefit.

membership.name: Health Law Advocates
membership.primaryEvidence: Health Law Advocates' MHAP for Kids page says lawyers serve every Massachusetts county to secure mental-health and education services; broader initiatives include coverage and parity. Official site names HLA and EIN and links a giving form. Clinical follow-through and government funding counterfactual remain open.

membership.name: Health Care For All
membership.primaryEvidence: Health Care For All uses a help line, enrollment support and policy campaigns to improve Massachusetts coverage/access; current primary site and donor page name HCFA. Statewide eligibility/policy affects the five MA MSA counties, not NH; HLA is a separate recipient despite related missions.

membership.name: Massachusetts Law Reform Institute
membership.primaryEvidence: MLRI's current site describes statewide poverty-law reform, tenant/benefits protections and maintained legal-aid resources. Its giving page specifies MLRI EIN. Local effect must be allocated among the five MA MSA counties and separated from direct-provider effects.

membership.name: Massachusetts Advocates for Children
membership.primaryEvidence: Massachusetts Advocates for Children offers education-rights helpline, family/professional training and policy advocacy across MA. Its official giving page names MAC and EIN. Educational outcomes require defensible mental-health/welfare translation; no automatic lifetime earnings/QALY conversion.

membership.name: Massachusetts Coalition for the Homeless
membership.primaryEvidence: Massachusetts Coalition for the Homeless identifies housing/benefits policy, family supports and current health-related social-needs services, based in Lynn. Official giving page confirms named charity support. Statewide scope intersects MA counties, but furniture provision or laws passed are not health-effect measures.

membership.name: Pine Street Inn
membership.primaryEvidence: Pine Street Inn describes Boston homeless outreach, shelter, supportive housing and recovery/employment services. Its ways-to-give page identifies the nonprofit and EIN. A hosted checkout was in scheduled maintenance; parent giving instructions remain live and no completed transaction is claimed.

membership.name: Rosie's Place
membership.primaryEvidence: Rosie's Place describes Boston women's shelter, meals, wellness, legal/housing and education support; its giving page explicitly says it does not accept city/state/federal support. This strengthens gift sensitivity, not evidence of superior clinical effectiveness.

membership.name: Bridge Over Troubled Waters
membership.primaryEvidence: Bridge provides Boston youth ages 14-24 crisis access, shelter and supportive services at 47 West Street, with a named donation route. Youth stabilization is plausible; broad client success or testimony is not a causal health estimate.

membership.name: HomeStart
membership.primaryEvidence: HomeStart lists Boston eviction-prevention hotline and housing stabilization, with official donation/EIN. Prevention rather than shelter-bed creation is its comparative mechanism. The homepage has conflicting hybrid/walk-in notices; no unconditional current walk-in access is asserted.

membership.name: Heading Home
membership.primaryEvidence: Heading Home describes Eastern MA family shelter, supportive housing, prevention, financial and clinical services, with Boston headquarters and current local program mission. Its giving page supports the whole recipient. Housing-retention claims are descriptive, not causal effectiveness. Final locality check: current locations-served page explicitly lists Boston and other eligible communities, separately from Fall River, New Bedford, Taunton and Worcester.

membership.name: FamilyAid
membership.primaryEvidence: FamilyAid explicitly serves Greater Boston children/parents through homelessness prevention, shelter and housing placement; current site names EIN and giving route. Its recent large restricted gift is a funding-counterfactual lead, not proof ordinary donations have no value or no gap.

membership.name: Father Bill's and MainSpring
membership.primaryEvidence: Father Bill's and MainSpring identifies Quincy and Brockton shelter/housing resource centers, prevention, diversion and supportive housing, with current Plymouth expansion. Official giving page names one combined recipient/EIN. Do not count the two historical names independently.

membership.name: Housing Families
membership.primaryEvidence: Housing Families identifies Malden-based Greater Boston family shelter, eviction legal aid, mental-health and supportive housing services, with explicit EIN and donation page. Spoonfuls food partnership creates potential double counting, not a second health gain per delivered item.

membership.name: Somerville Homeless Coalition
membership.primaryEvidence: Somerville Homeless Coalition reports relocated Somerville service offices, shelter, food and eviction-prevention programs, with named giving page/EIN. Animated counters rendered as zero are ignored; no numeric output estimate is inferred from them.

membership.name: On The Rise
membership.primaryEvidence: On The Rise provides a Cambridge daytime safe haven, relationship-based advocacy and housing retention for women/trans/nonbinary adults. Official ways-to-give page identifies payee and EIN. Reported retention is uncontrolled and may reflect other housing supports.

membership.name: Solutions at Work
membership.primaryEvidence: Solutions at Work's current Cambridge site lists children's-item exchange and professional-attire programs and an explicit donor route. This is a basic-needs/employment pathway, not verified current clinical or shelter operation. Exact EIN is available on request but not recovered here.

membership.name: Women's Lunch Place
membership.primaryEvidence: Women's Lunch Place describes Boston meals, housing stabilization, shelter-to-housing and on-site physical/mental care; giving page names EIN. Partner-delivered clinical resources must be reconciled and benefits not duplicated with BHCHP or other agencies.

membership.name: Project Place
membership.primaryEvidence: Project Place lists Boston employment skills, case management, housing help and social enterprises; linked Qgiv form explicitly names Project Place. The health pathway is indirect through stability and income; not all employment or enterprise revenue is a welfare gain.

membership.name: St Francis House
membership.primaryEvidence: St Francis House lists Boston behavioral, housing, nutrition and employment services and names BHCHP as its on-site medical operator. Official giving page/EIN identify SFH. Clinical effects must not be fully attributed to both SFH and BHCHP.

membership.name: Action Inc
membership.primaryEvidence: Action Inc. has Gloucester housing/shelter, benefits, heating and weatherization services plus Peabody energy office; official giving page names EIN. Public energy grants and utility-program resources must remain in the full-resource counterfactual.

membership.name: Community Teamwork
membership.primaryEvidence: Community Teamwork identifies itself as Greater Lowell's Community Action Agency, with housing, energy, behavioral and nutrition supports. Named giving page/EIN are current. Public subsidies/program totals do not establish private-gift marginal output.

membership.name: Community Servings
membership.primaryEvidence: Community Servings' current meal page specifies medically tailored, dietitian-prescribed weekly meals for critically/chronically ill and food-insecure MA/RI residents, prepared in Boston. All five MA counties are eligible; RI and any nonresident benefit are excluded locally. Giving route is current.

membership.name: Project Bread
membership.primaryEvidence: Project Bread connects Massachusetts residents to federal nutrition programs and operates food-access policy/healthcare initiatives. Official site names EIN and giving route. Statewide availability covers the five MA counties; benefit dollars are transfers, not equal-dollar net social value.

membership.name: Greater Boston Food Bank
membership.primaryEvidence: Greater Boston Food Bank explicitly distributes food across Eastern Massachusetts and offers SNAP enrollment support, with official giving/EIN. Eligible five MA counties are a service intersection, not an exhaustive catchment or beneficiary fraction; do not add food-bank and pantry benefit counts.

membership.name: Food For Free
membership.primaryEvidence: Food For Free identifies Greater Boston food recovery/transport, direct student/senior programs and Somerville distribution center, with official EIN/giving page. Its minimum local operational footprint is Middlesex; recipient-pantry and bank overlap must be adjusted.

membership.name: Spoonfuls
membership.primaryEvidence: Spoonfuls lists food recovery/distribution to regional community organizations, current Newton headquarters, and an official giving page for fleet/staff operations. Its partner listing includes local agencies, and Housing Families confirms partnership. Waste/climate and food benefits need separate, nonduplicated measures.

membership.name: The Open Door
membership.primaryEvidence: The Open Door posts current Gloucester pantry, meals and SNAP help with explicit service hours and donation/EIN. It is one nonprofit including its thrift operation, not every meal/retail branch a distinct recipient.

membership.name: Citizens Inn
membership.primaryEvidence: Citizens Inn identifies family shelter, recovery/transitional housing and Haven from Hunger meals/pantry at Peabody; named giving page supports the combined organization. Haven from Hunger is not counted separately.

membership.name: Healthy Waltham
membership.primaryEvidence: Healthy Waltham's official indexed site/giving page identifies current Waltham food access and vulnerable-resident wellness, plus named NeonCRM donor link. Direct pages returned 403 but primary indexed text was reviewed; no invented output counts or EIN.

membership.name: Merrimack Valley Food Bank
membership.primaryEvidence: Merrimack Valley Food Bank describes Greater Lowell food rescue, mobile nutrition for homebound elders, school food and SNAP assistance. Official giving page and EIN are explicit. Broader Merrimack Valley/NH reach is not automatically inside this MSA.

membership.name: Conservation Law Foundation
membership.primaryEvidence: CLF's Massachusetts page identifies pollution accountability, transit, climate/energy and environmental-health work; official giving page names CLF and EIN. New England-wide portfolio costs remain whole-recipient; only Boston-MSA policy/exposure benefits count locally.

membership.name: Clean Water Fund
membership.primaryEvidence: Clean Water Fund's own MA page and MA giving page identify education/research for pollution, lead/toxics and energy health, EIN 52-1043444. The separate 501(c)(4) Clean Water Action route is explicitly not the counted recipient. Joint campaigns require role/cost allocation before health credit.

membership.name: GreenRoots
membership.primaryEvidence: GreenRoots' current official domain identifies Chelsea/East Boston environmental-health, heat/flood resilience, air/energy and food-justice campaigns. It links gifts to GreenRoots Inc. and explicitly locates benefits in those communities. Old domain's empty response is not positive evidence.

membership.name: Alternatives for Community and Environment
membership.primaryEvidence: ACE identifies Roxbury organizing, legal/policy assistance, environmental justice, transit and displacement work, with official giving page. Providence and wider-MA activity are outside the local numerator unless eligible residents are verified; coalition wins need attribution.

membership.name: LivableStreets Alliance
membership.primaryEvidence: LivableStreets identifies practical Metro Boston transportation advocacy, Vision Zero and Blue Hill Avenue bus/street work, with named donation page and Cambridge office. Injury/exposure changes are plausible, not measured; mode-shift harms, displacement and government implementation are future alpha gates.

membership.name: MassBike
membership.primaryEvidence: MassBike's official about page describes statewide safer-cycling law, education and design advocacy, and its donor form states tax deductibility. MA law applicability includes five local counties. Worcester e-bike outcomes and statewide event attendance are not Boston health gains.

membership.name: Greater Seacoast Health (Greater Seacoast Community Health)
membership.primaryEvidence: Greater Seacoast Health's history confirms 2018 merger of Goodwin and Families First into Greater Seacoast Community Health, renamed brand in 2026, with Portsmouth/Somersworth care. Both NH counties qualify; former brands count once. SOS Recovery is now independent but not separately counted in this set.

membership.name: Lamprey Health Care
membership.primaryEvidence: Lamprey lists active Newmarket and Raymond clinical services, substance-use, chronic-disease and primary care plus a donation page. Nashua is in Hillsborough and excluded; all recipient expenses remain relevant to an unrestricted gift.

membership.name: Seacoast Mental Health Center
membership.primaryEvidence: Seacoast Mental Health Center lists Portsmouth/Exeter clinics, youth/adult/older-adult mental-health and crisis services, with official giving instructions/EIN. NH rapid-response network is not wholly the center's own output or a new charity.

membership.name: HAVEN
membership.primaryEvidence: HAVEN explicitly serves Rockingham and Strafford counties, with Portsmouth/Rochester locations and survivor advocacy, hotline, shelter and education. Official donor page distinguishes capital campaign from annual fund and names EIN. No entire-NH beneficiary claim is used.

membership.name: Cross Roads House
membership.primaryEvidence: Cross Roads House provides Portsmouth emergency shelter and supports return to permanent housing, with official donor payee, address and EIN. Wider Seacoast residents may be outside the MSA; only eligible resident benefits count.
